# Rule reference

<!-- Generated by `radguard rules --markdown`. tests/test_rules.py fails if this file is out of date. -->

RadGuard reports 80 rules. Every finding names its rule, and SARIF reports link each result to its rule's section here. The severity shown is the usual one; a finding can be more or less severe in context, as each description says.

| Kind | What to do |
|---|---|
| malware | Quarantine the file and keep it away from anything that could run or extract the embedded content. Extract the payload at the reported offset for malware analysis, find out how the file entered the archive, and check other files from the same source. Re-saving the file in a viewer is not a fix: it may keep the payload, and it destroys evidence. |
| hidden-data | Extract the bytes at the reported offset (`radguard map` shows the file's layout) and identify them. Conforming software never stores data where readers do not look, so the content is either a writer bug or deliberately hidden. |
| differential | Different DICOM software can read this file differently, so no single viewer's rendering can be trusted. Compare what the viewer, the PACS and any AI pipeline actually show; to normalise the study, re-acquire it from the source, or rewrite it with a strict toolkit and scan it again. |
| memory-safety | Open the file only with current, sandboxed decoders: this is the input class behind decoder memory-safety bugs. Quarantine it and trace its source, because crafted headers like this rarely occur by accident. |
| resource | The file is built to exhaust the resources of software that processes it. Quarantine it, and check whether any system that ingested it (PACS, router, AI pipeline) slowed down or failed. |
| incomplete | Part of the file was not inspected, so the verdict for it is partial. Inspect the reported range with other tools. A file that deliberately exhausts analysis budgets should be treated as hostile. |
| conformance | Usually a buggy or non-conforming writer rather than an attack. Note the producing software (Implementation Class UID and Version Name in the File Meta Information) and report the defect to its vendor if it recurs. |

## Preamble

### preamble.archive

**7z or RAR archive header in the preamble**. severity **medium**, precision high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. Archive tools that identify files by their first bytes open it as an archive.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.elf-polyglot

**ELF executable header in the preamble**. severity **critical**, precision very-high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. An ELF header needs only its magic at byte 0, so the file runs on Linux-based devices while remaining a valid image (ELFDICOM).

References: <https://www.praetorian.com/blog/elfdicom-poc-malware-polyglot-exploiting-linux-based-medical-devices/>

### preamble.fat-or-class

**Mach-O universal binary or Java class header in the preamble**. severity **high**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. Both formats start with CA FE BA BE; either makes the file loadable as code.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.macho-polyglot

**Mach-O executable header in the preamble**. severity **critical**, precision very-high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. The file can be loaded as a macOS executable while remaining a valid image.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.markup

**HTML, XML or SVG markup in the preamble**. severity **high**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. Browsers and content sniffers treat the file as markup, which runs script (HTML, SVG) when the file is opened or served from a web context.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.mz-header

**DOS/PE header in the preamble**. severity **high**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code.

The preamble starts with an MZ header, but e_lfanew does not point at a PE signature, so the file is not runnable as it stands. No imaging software writes MZ into the preamble: this is usually a truncated or staged PE/DICOM polyglot.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.nonstandard

**Unrecognised non-zero preamble**. severity **low**, precision medium, kind hidden-data.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, but nearly all software writes zeros or a TIFF header. Unrecognised content is not evidence of an attack on its own; it is worth identifying because it is what other programs see first.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part10/chapter_7.html>

### preamble.ole

**OLE compound file header in the preamble**. severity **high**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. The format of MSI installers and legacy Office documents, both of which can carry code.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.pdf

**PDF header in the preamble**. severity **medium**, precision high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. PDF readers accept a header anywhere in the first kilobyte, so the file also opens as a document.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.pe-polyglot

**Windows executable in the preamble (PE/DICOM polyglot)**. severity **critical**, precision very-high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The preamble starts with an MZ header whose e_lfanew field points at a real PE signature further into the file, so the same bytes are a valid image and a runnable Windows program (CVE-2019-11687). Viewers display it normally, and because it is "just a scan" it often escapes malware inspection.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.rtf

**RTF header in the preamble**. severity **medium**, precision high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. Word processors open the file as an RTF document, a format with a long history of exploited parser bugs.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.shebang

**Script interpreter line in the preamble**. severity **high**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. A file that starts with #!/ runs as a script on Unix-like systems once it is marked executable.

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

### preamble.zip

**ZIP container header in the preamble**. severity **high**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The 128-byte preamble is the first thing any non-DICOM program reads, and PS3.10 leaves it free for application use, so it can make one file two formats at once. Tools that identify files by their first bytes treat it as a ZIP-based container (JAR, APK, Office).

References: <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-11687>

## Structure

### structure.analysis-incomplete

**Part of the file was not inspected**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind incomplete.

A carving budget was reached. Either the file is larger than the inspection window (low), or it holds a flood of decoy signatures built to exhaust analysis (high). The range that was not inspected is reported, so it is never mistaken for clean.

### structure.bad-fragment-item

**Corrupt pixel data fragment**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Frame decoders resynchronise differently.

### structure.bad-offset-table

**Basic Offset Table points outside the fragments**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Decoders that seek frames through the table read the wrong bytes.

### structure.bad-sequence-item

**Corrupt sequence**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Different DICOM readers will interpret these bytes differently.

### structure.deflate-bomb

**Decompression bomb**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind resource, [CWE-409](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html) Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification).

The deflated dataset expands far beyond any real image.

### structure.deflate-error

**Corrupt deflate stream**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The dataset cannot be decoded.

### structure.deflate-truncated

**Truncated deflate stream**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers recover different amounts of the dataset.

### structure.delimiter-length

**Delimiter with non-zero length**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers that honour the length skip extra bytes.

### structure.duplicate-tag

**Duplicate attribute**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers keep either the first or the last copy, so different software sees different values.

### structure.element-limit

**Too many elements**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind resource, [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html) Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling.

Element floods exhaust memory in parsers that build a full object tree.

### structure.group-length-mismatch

**Group length is wrong**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict, [CWE-130](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/130.html) Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency.

Readers that use group lengths to skip groups will skip a different range of bytes.

### structure.hidden-payload

**File hidden outside the DICOM structure**. severity **critical**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code.

Bytes the DICOM structure cannot account for contain a recognised file format, typically an executable appended after the dataset or left behind a broken element. DICOM readers never display these bytes; other programs can run or extract them. High rather than critical when the payload is an archive, a script or a document rather than an executable.

### structure.invalid-vr

**Invalid VR**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Compliant parsers stop or desynchronise here, so nothing after it is visible to them.

### structure.length-overflow

**Declared length exceeds its container**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind memory-safety, [CWE-130](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/130.html) Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, [CWE-125](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/125.html) Out-of-bounds Read.

Decoders that trust declared lengths read past the end of their buffer, the trigger for a long line of DICOM viewer memory-safety bugs.

### structure.max-depth

**Sequences nested too deeply**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind resource, [CWE-674](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/674.html) Uncontrolled Recursion.

Recursive parsers can be driven to stack exhaustion (denial of service).

### structure.meta-group-length-mismatch

**File Meta group length is wrong**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict, [CWE-130](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/130.html) Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency.

Readers that trust the length and readers that scan by group disagree on where the dataset, and its transfer syntax, begins.

### structure.missing-item-delimiter

**Unterminated item**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers disagree about where the item ends.

### structure.missing-meta-group-length

**File Meta group length missing**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind conformance.

Required by PS3.10; some readers mis-locate the dataset without it.

### structure.missing-sequence-delimiter

**Unterminated sequence**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers disagree about where the sequence ends.

### structure.missing-transfer-syntax

**No transfer syntax**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers must guess how the dataset is encoded.

### structure.no-part10-header

**No DICOM Part 10 header**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Strict readers reject the file but lenient ones (pydicom's force mode, many toolkits) read it, so tools that only look for the DICM marker skip it entirely.

### structure.nonzero-padding

**Data hidden in trailing padding**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel.

(FFFC,FFFC) Data Set Trailing Padding has no meaning (PS3.10 7.2) and readers skip it unread, so non-zero content in it is invisible to every DICOM tool. High or critical when it contains a recognised file.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part10/chapter_7.html>

### structure.odd-length

**Odd value length**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

PS3.5 requires even lengths; different DICOM readers will interpret these bytes differently.

### structure.reserved-nonzero

**Reserved header bytes are not zero**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel.

A covert channel that strict readers reject.

### structure.stray-delimiter

**Delimiter outside its structure**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Different DICOM readers will interpret these bytes differently.

### structure.suppressed

**Anomaly flood**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind incomplete.

A file that trips the same rule thousands of times is built to flood analysis; only the first occurrences are reported.

### structure.tag-order

**Attributes out of order**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers that stop early or search by tag will miss attributes that others see.

### structure.transfer-syntax-mismatch

**Transfer syntax does not match the encoding**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Lenient readers silently switch encodings and strict ones fail, so the same file decodes differently depending on the software.

### structure.truncated-header

**File ends mid-element**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind conformance.

Usually an interrupted transfer.

### structure.undefined-fragment-length

**Pixel data fragment with undefined length**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Not allowed; decoders cannot find the fragment's end.

### structure.undefined-length-invalid

**Undefined length on a non-sequence attribute**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers have no way to find where the value ends.

### structure.unexpected-delimiter

**Sequence delimiter inside a defined-length sequence**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers that honour the delimiter end the sequence early.

### structure.unexplained-bytes

**Bytes not accounted for by the DICOM structure**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel.

Every byte of a conforming file belongs to the preamble, the magic, an element header or a value. These bytes belong to none of them, so no reader displays them. Severity grows with size: low under 16 bytes, medium under 1 KiB, high above.

### structure.unknown-transfer-syntax

**Non-standard transfer syntax**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind conformance.

Most software cannot decode it; may indicate a private or crafted encoding.

### structure.unterminated-pixel-data

**Encapsulated pixel data not terminated**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Decoders disagree about where the last frame ends.

### structure.vr-length-mismatch

**Value length does not fit its VR**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Readers disagree on how many values there are and may read partial values.

### structure.vr-mismatch

**Attribute encoded with the wrong VR**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Dictionary-driven and header-driven readers decode different values from the same bytes.

## Pixel data

### pixels.ambiguous-geometry

**Conflicting image dimensions**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Rows, Columns, Samples per Pixel, Number of Frames or Bits Allocated appears more than once with different values, so readers that keep different copies decode the same pixel bytes with different dimensions.

### pixels.analysis-incomplete

**Frames beyond the inspection budget**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind incomplete.

Compressed frames beyond the per-file reassembly budget were not inspected.

### pixels.codec-mismatch

**Frame is not the codec its transfer syntax declares**. severity **high**, precision high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

A frame does not start with its codec's start marker, so decoders either fail or, if they sniff the content, decode something else. Critical when the frame is an executable.

### pixels.codestream-trailing-data

**Data after the end of a compressed frame**. severity **high**, precision high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel.

Decoders stop at a codestream's end marker, so bytes after it are never displayed: a second hidden image, or an executable. Medium for a few unexplained bytes, critical for an executable.

### pixels.duplicate-pixel-data

**Two images in one file**. severity **critical**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The dataset has more than one Pixel Data element. Software that keeps the first copy and software that keeps the last display different images from the same file, so a radiologist's viewer and an AI pipeline can be shown different scans.

### pixels.embedded-file

**File stored as image pixels**. severity **critical**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code.

The declared image area contains a recognised file format. Viewers render it as noise, and nothing that only displays images will notice. Severity follows what was found: critical for executables.

### pixels.encoding-mismatch

**Pixel Data encoding contradicts the transfer syntax**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Compressed transfer syntaxes require encapsulated Pixel Data and native ones require a single value. A mismatch sends decoders down different code paths for the same bytes.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_A.4.html>

### pixels.hidden-frames

**More frames than declared**. severity **high**, precision high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Encapsulated Pixel Data holds more frames than Number of Frames declares; decoders that trust the header show fewer frames than decoders that walk the fragments.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_A.4.html>

### pixels.invalid-geometry

**Zero or negative image dimension**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind memory-safety, [CWE-1284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1284.html) Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input.

The image header declares a zero or negative dimension (Number of Frames is text, so "0" or "-5" is easy to write). Decoders disagree on what, if anything, to render, and size arithmetic on such values is a classic source of decoder bugs.

### pixels.malformed-codestream

**Malformed compressed frame**. severity **medium**, precision high, kind memory-safety.

A JPEG, JPEG-LS, JPEG 2000 or RLE frame breaks its own format's structure. Malformed codestreams are the input class behind many image decoder memory-safety bugs.

### pixels.missing-frames

**Fewer frames than declared**. severity **medium**, precision high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Encapsulated Pixel Data holds fewer frames than Number of Frames declares; decoders that trust the header look for frames that are not there.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_A.4.html>

### pixels.multiple-representations

**Integer and floating-point pixel data in one file**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Pixel Data and (Double) Float Pixel Data are mutually exclusive; which one is displayed depends on the software.

### pixels.size-overflow

**Image size overflows 32-bit arithmetic**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind memory-safety, [CWE-190](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/190.html) Integer Overflow or Wraparound, [CWE-787](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html) Out-of-bounds Write.

Rows x Columns x Samples x Frames x Bits needs 4 GiB or more. A decoder that computes the size in 32 bits allocates a small buffer and then writes the full image into it: a heap overflow.

### pixels.slack

**Data after the last pixel**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Pixel Data is longer than the image the header describes. Viewers that honour the header never display the extra bytes, while lenient decoders (pydicom among them) return them as extra frames: hidden data, or a hidden image. Severity rises with size, entropy and recognised content.

### pixels.truncated

**Pixel Data shorter than the image it describes**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind memory-safety, [CWE-130](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/130.html) Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, [CWE-125](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/125.html) Out-of-bounds Read.

Decoders that trust the header read past the end of the pixel buffer.

## Attribute values

### values.document-payload

**Executable inside an encapsulated document**. severity **critical**, precision very-high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code.

An Encapsulated Document (0042,0011), meant to hold a PDF, CDA or similar report, contains an executable.

### values.document-type-mismatch

**Encapsulated document is not what it claims**. severity **high**, precision high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The declared MIME type and the content disagree: software that trusts the declared type and software that sniffs the content handle the document differently.

### values.document-type-missing

**Encapsulated document without a MIME type**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

The document has no MIME Type of Encapsulated Document (0042,0012), so viewers must guess how to open it.

### values.embedded-file

**File embedded in an attribute value**. severity **critical**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code.

A recognised file format sits inside an attribute value: a private blob, an unknown-VR value, an item deep in a sequence. Executables have no business in any attribute (critical), scripts are high and archives medium; documents and markup are routine vendor practice and reported as low for review.

## Private data

### private.analysis-incomplete

**Compressed private data built to exhaust analysis**. severity **high**, precision very-high, kind incomplete.

The decompressed content of a private value floods the signature search with decoys, so part of it could not be inspected.

### private.compressed-payload

**File hidden inside compressed private data**. severity **critical**, precision high, kind malware, [CWE-506](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/506.html) Embedded Malicious Code.

A zlib or gzip private value decompresses to data containing a recognised file format. Compression hides it from any signature search of the file itself.

### private.creator-invalid

**Malformed Private Creator**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind conformance.

A Private Creator is empty, not LO, too long or contains control characters, so readers that match creators by name cannot recognise the block.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_7.8.html>

### private.data-after-stream

**Data hidden after a compressed stream**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel.

Bytes follow the end of a compressed private value. Decompressors stop at the end of the stream, so nothing that reads the value normally sees them.

### private.decompression-bomb

**Compressed private data too large to inspect**. severity **high**, precision high, kind resource, [CWE-409](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html) Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification).

A compressed private value expands more than 1000:1, past the per-value limit or past the per-file budget. That is a decompression bomb aimed at tools that inflate private data, or data built to exceed analysis budgets; the part that was not inspected is not reported clean.

### private.duplicate-creator

**Private Creator reserves two blocks**. severity **low**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

One creator name reserves two blocks of the same group; readers that look a creator up by name find one block or the other.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_7.8.html>

### private.illegal-group

**Private element in a forbidden group**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind differential, [CWE-436](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/436.html) Interpretation Conflict.

Groups 0001, 0003, 0005, 0007 and FFFF may not carry private data (PS3.5 7.8.1); readers disagree on whether such elements are standard or private.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_7.8.html>

### private.opaque-blob

**High-entropy private data of unknown format**. severity **medium**, precision medium, kind hidden-data.

At least 4 KiB of private binary data at 7.5 bits/byte or more that matches no known format: that is how encrypted or compressed data looks, and nothing in the file explains it. Vendors do store proprietary compressed data, so this is a lead for review rather than proof.

### private.orphan-element

**Private data with no creator**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel.

No Private Creator reserves the block this element sits in, so no software can attribute it and every tool ignores it.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_7.8.html>

### private.unusable-element

**Private element outside any reservable block**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind hidden-data, [CWE-514](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/514.html) Covert Channel.

Only Private Creators (gggg,0010-00FF) and private data elements (gggg,1000-FFFF) are defined, so no reader can interpret an element elsewhere in a private group, and every reader skips it.

References: <https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part05/sect_7.8.html>

## Scan

### scan.findings-suppressed

**Finding flood suppressed**. severity **medium**, precision very-high, kind incomplete.

One file produced more findings for one rule than the per-rule cap; the first ones are kept and the rest are counted. A file that trips the same rule thousands of times is usually built to flood the report.
